newsitem.title: USA: Shell says pact with Texaco will benefit market.
newsitem.headline: Shell says pact with Texaco will benefit market.

text.p: Shell Oil Co said Friday that the planned merging of its western U.S. refining and marketing operations with Texaco would benefit retail and wholesale gasoline sellers, customers and shareholders.
"The primary goal in creating such an alliance is to build a competitive downstream company," the company, a U.S. unit of Royal Dutch/Shell, said in a statement.
The statement was issued after a filing by five consumer groups urging the Federal Trade Commission to block the proposed combination.
The groups said a combined Shell-Texaco company on the West Coast would create a new giant in a market that was already dominated by just a few companies.

Matching earlier comments by a Texaco spokesman, Shell said it believed "a combination of assets will enable the companies to achieve the operating efficiencies and optimize the brand strengths necessary to succeed in the extremely difficult downstream environment."
Shell focused on the fact that, nationally, the combined company would have less than 13 percent of U.S. refining capacity and less than 15 percent of branded gasoline sales.

However, the consumer groups said the FTC should focus on local markets, particularly on the West Coast, where the combined company would have 18 percent of the gasoline market and 23 percent of refining capacity.
